I've taken a look at the new autoformalized PR. As far as I can tell, it doesn't rely on use of the Whitney Lemma as proved in PR #227 at all. We had suspected from earlier discussions that perhaps the Whitney Lemma wasn't exactly what was needed for a short cut anyway. The statement in the code of the lemma (with sorry for proof) is in # Generalising SchwartzMap.compCLM#176, which is what PR#227 is based off. Because #176 was never itself merged to main, it was not I believe in the base from which the autoformalizer is based.

As a result, I think:

  1. There is no real purpose of merging PR#227 (or #176) into the code.
  2. There is some other work in #176 as well, I'm not certain about whether that might be duplicative with the new PR or not, it might be interesting to see if there is anything there.
  3. PR#227 is of its own intrinsic interest still, perhaps something that would be worthwhile upstreaming to mathlib, although the proof itself stills needs a lot of work. @Cameron Freer has already done some work on golfing/improving it, which I think makes sense to merge into it already.

So, my proposal would be to close PR#227 (and probably #176) out of the repo, and but keep the statement of the Whitney (and Borel) Lemma's in it, perhaps in a new repo with a goal of getting them in shape to upstream to mathlib? Would welcome thoughts from @Sidharth Hariharan and @Cameron Freer as well as anyone else.
Could you point out which file/directory of Gauss' PR might be relevant?

Thanks for taking a look at this, @Matthew Cushman. I also took a look along with @Auguste Poiroux and it's not immediately clear to us how the Gauss PR does either something analogous or routes around it. In any case, we agree that it's probably not worth merging spherepacking#227 insofar as it is not strictly needed, and also that it may still be of independent interest / worth refining elsewhere for other reasons.

To Seewoo's question, I think the closest thing (at least that I could find) is this: https://github.com/math-inc/Sphere-Packing-Lean/blob/gauss/SpherePacking/ForMathlib/RadialSchwartz/OneSided.lean

This seems very similar to the approach that @Sidharth Hariharan and I were discussing a couple of packathons ago, but it's a sort of converse to the Whitney lemma (and much simpler to prove)

Yes, this looks a lot like what we were discussing - especially the multiplication by a cutoff trick. I think the Whitney Lemma is still helpful to have in Mathlib, so if you want you can keep a working copy of it here, but it may indeed be better to just fork mathlib and make a PR there.
(Apologies for the late response, was on spring break last week)
